Regional replication percentage along genome-wide replication progress

Source: R/tempo.R
rep_tempo.Rd

For every target region, averages the replication state of the overlapping bins within each cell and then averages cells within groups ordered by genome-wide replication progress. Bins contribute equally whenever they overlap a target (strand is ignored). Missing bins are excluded within each cell; cells without an observed bin are excluded from their group's mean.

Usage

rep_tempo(
  rep_matrix,
  granges,
  ncells = NULL,
  bin_granges = NULL,
  cell_rep_percent = NULL,
  meta_data = NULL,
  var_use = "rep_percent",
  nbin_rep = NULL,
  unrep_state = 2,
  rep_state = 4
)

Arguments

rep_matrix

Numeric matrix or Matrix, bins by cells, holding unrep_state, rep_state and NA only. Row and column names must be unique bin and cell IDs.

granges

GRanges of target regions. IDs are taken from the range_id column, names(granges), the iz_id column, or the coordinates, in that order.

ncells

Optional positive integer: consecutive cells per non-overlapping group (cells must then be sorted by progress). Mutually exclusive with nbin_rep. If neither is given each cell is its own group.

bin_granges

Optional GRanges with a bin_id column or names matching the matrix row names. Otherwise the row names are parsed as chr-start-end or chr:start-end.

cell_rep_percent

Optional numeric genome-wide progress in 0-100, named by cell ID or in matrix column order. Defaults to 100 times the column means of the recoded matrix. Do not combine with meta_data.

meta_data

Optional data.frame whose row names are cell IDs; its var_use column (finite, in 0-1) defines genome-wide progress.

var_use

Column of meta_data holding progress.

nbin_rep

Optional positive integer: number of equal-width progress intervals spanning 0-1. Cells in an interval are merged with equal weight; empty intervals stay as NA columns. Requires meta_data. Genome-wide analyses typically use nbin_rep = 100.

unrep_state, rep_state

Codes of the unreplicated and replicated states in rep_matrix. The defaults (2 and 4) are the codes written by assign_replication_states(). Use 0 and 1 for a matrix that is already binary.

Value

A data.frame (regions by progress groups) of percentages in 0-100. Attributes: rep_bins, range_info, cell_info, n_valid_cells and units. Save it with saveRDS() to keep the attributes, and subset it with subset_rep_tempo().

See also

fit_rep_tempo()
